title: Open ATS job posting
description: One open job posting, normalised across Greenhouse, Ashby and Lever into a single schema. Fields the vendor does not provide are null rather than guessed.

source.title: ATS
source.description: Which applicant tracking system this posting came from: greenhouse, ashby or lever.

company.title: Company
company.description: The company's board token on that ATS. It is the vendor's own identifier, so it is stable and joinable.

job_id.title: Job ID
job_id.description: The vendor's own posting ID. Unique within a company board, and stable across runs, so it is what you deduplicate on.

title.title: Title
title.description: The job title, exactly as the company wrote it.

location.title: Location
location.description: The location string as published. Not normalised — companies write it too many ways for a mapping to be honest.

workplace.title: Workplace
workplace.description: remote, hybrid or onsite. Taken from the vendor's own workplace field where one exists, and inferred from the location text otherwise.

department.title: Department
department.description: The department as published, e.g. Engineering, Sales. Null where the vendor does not carry one.

team.title: Team
team.description: The team within the department, where the ATS provides it.

employment_type.title: Employment type
employment_type.description: Full-time, contract, internship and so on, where the ATS provides it.

posted_at.title: Posted
posted_at.description: When the posting first went live, ISO 8601.

updated_at.title: Updated
updated_at.description: When the posting last changed, ISO 8601. This is what the postedSince filter compares against, so it is the field to poll on for a daily delta.

salary_min.title: Salary min
salary_min.description: Parsed from the published compensation range. Null when the company did not publish one — never estimated.

salary_max.title: Salary max
salary_max.description: Parsed from the published compensation range. Null when the company did not publish one — never estimated.

salary_currency.title: Currency
salary_currency.description: ISO currency code for the parsed range.

seniority.title: Seniority
seniority.description: intern, junior, mid, senior, principal or executive. Inferred from the title — it is a convenience, not a fact the company published.

description.title: Description
description.description: Full plain-text job description. Only present when includeDescription is on; it is roughly ten times the size of everything else.

record_type.title: Record type
record_type.description: Present and equal to company_signal on rows produced in signals mode. Absent on job postings.

signal.title: Signal
signal.description: ramping (3+ roles opened in the last 30 days, at 2x or more the pace of the prior 60), new_board (nothing on the board older than 60 days), steady, quiet (open roles but none opened in 30 days), or undated (this ATS published no dates for this board).

open_postings.title: Open roles
open_postings.description: How many roles this company has open right now, after your filters.

postings_dated.title: Dated roles
postings_dated.description: How many of those carry a publication date. Every window below is computed against this number, not against open roles, so an undated board is never silently counted as a quiet one.

opened_7d.title: Opened 7d
opened_7d.description: Roles first published in the last 7 days.

opened_30d.title: Opened 30d
opened_30d.description: Roles first published in the last 30 days.

opened_90d.title: Opened 90d
opened_90d.description: Roles first published in the last 90 days.

baseline_30d.title: Baseline 30d
baseline_30d.description: The company's own prior pace: roles opened in the 60 days before the last 30, expressed per 30 days. This is the number the last month is being compared against.

ramp_ratio.title: Ramp
ramp_ratio.description: Opened 30d divided by the baseline. 2.0 means the company is hiring at twice its own recent pace. Null when there is no prior baseline to divide by — a board with no postings older than 30 days is a new board, not an infinite ramp.

new_functions.title: Newly opened functions
new_functions.description: Departments where every currently-open role was opened in the last 45 days, at a company whose board also carries older roles — the "they just opened a sales function" signal. Two limits stated plainly: only open roles are visible, so this is evidence a function is being staffed now rather than proof it did not exist before; and it is suppressed entirely on boards carrying more than 25 distinct departments, because those use the field as a site or sub-team code and a new function cannot be told from a new location.

top_departments.title: Departments
top_departments.description: The five departments with the most open roles, largest first.

top_titles.title: Repeated titles
top_titles.description: The five most repeated job titles on the board. A title opened many times over is usually a team being built rather than a backfill.

tech_signals.title: Technologies
tech_signals.description: Technologies named in roles opened in the last 90 days, most-mentioned first. Matched on whole words from a conservative list — an ambiguous term produces a wrong signal, so terms like "Go" and "R" are deliberately not matched.

executive_openings_90d.title: Exec openings 90d
executive_openings_90d.description: Head-of / VP / C-level roles opened in the last 90 days. Seniority is inferred from the title.

remote_postings.title: Remote roles
remote_postings.description: How many of the open roles are remote.

postings_with_salary.title: Roles with salary
postings_with_salary.description: How many of the open roles publish a compensation range we could parse unambiguously.

oldest_posting_at.title: Oldest role
oldest_posting_at.description: Publication date of the oldest role still open, ISO 8601.

newest_posting_at.title: Newest role
newest_posting_at.description: Publication date of the most recently opened role, ISO 8601.

index_as_of.title: Index date
index_as_of.description: The date the company index was last swept. Boards open and close; the postings themselves are always fetched live at run time.

fetched_at.title: Fetched
fetched_at.description: When this run read the board.
